papers.title: stFormer integrates spatial ligand signaling into a foundation model for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Recent foundation models for single-cell transcriptomic data generate informative, context-aware gene and cell representations. Spatial transcriptomic (ST) data offer extra positional insights but were not considered by these single-cell models. We introduce stFormer, a transformer model tailored for ST data, which employs the cross-attention module to incorporate spatial ligand genes. To unify different ST technologies with a trade-off between resolution and gene coverage, we propose a biased cross-attention method that enables the model to do learning with single-cell resolution on whole-tra
papers.summary: stFormer is a transformer-based foundation model designed specifically for spatial transcriptomics data, using cross-attention to incorporate spatial ligand signaling information. It introduces a biased cross-attention method to unify different spatial transcriptomics technologies, balancing resolution and gene coverage, and enables single-cell resolution learning on whole-transcriptome data.

papers.title: AcrSeek: Metric Learning with Hybrid Negative Mining for Anti-CRISPR Protein Detection under Extreme Class Imbalance.
papers.abstract: Anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are key targets for precise control of CRISPR-based genome editing and phage-host coevolution research. Their experimental identification is costly and low-throughput, so computational predictors are used to prioritise candidates for testing. In this setting validated positives number in the hundreds while phage-derived putative negatives reach tens of thousands, producing extreme class imbalance. Yet existing classification-based predictors train and evaluate on 1:1 balanced datasets and allow high-similarity sequences between trainin
papers.summary: AcrSeek is a new computational tool for detecting anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins, which inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are useful for controlling genome editing. Unlike existing predictors that train on artificially balanced datasets, AcrSeek uses metric learning with hybrid negative mining to handle the extreme class imbalance (hundreds of positives vs. tens of thousands of negatives) and high sequence similarity typical of real-world data. This makes it better suited for prioritizing candidate Acr proteins for experimental testing.

papers.title: Post-Search Validation and Curation of Site-Resolved N‑Glycoproteomics Data.
papers.abstract: Given the significant role of glycosylation in modulating protein structure and activity, glycoproteomics is gaining increased interest from the broad scientific community. Large-scale site-resolved N-glycoproteomics relies on automated MS2-based searches, but candidate glycopeptide assignments can remain ambiguous when isomeric or isobaric glycan structures, adducts, chemical modifications, in-source fragments, or incomplete MS2 evidence support more than one plausible interpretation. Here, we systematically categorize common challenges and misassignments in glycoproteomics and present a post
papers.summary: This paper systematically catalogs common pitfalls and misassignments in large-scale site-resolved N-glycoproteomics, where automated MS2 searches can produce ambiguous glycopeptide identifications due to isomeric or isobaric glycans, adducts, modifications, and incomplete fragmentation evidence. The authors propose a post-search validation and curation framework to help researchers distinguish correct assignments from plausible but incorrect alternatives.

papers.title: Enhanced Sampling of Protein Conformations in AlphaFold3 with Repulsive Bias in the Diffusion Generative Model.
papers.abstract: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3 (AF3), to predict. It has been observed that AF3 sometimes fails to capture ligand-induced conformational changes, even though it explicitly includes ligand molecules that induce such changes. To address this challenge, we develop an enhanced sampling scheme that leverages the diffusion-based generative model used in AF3 to predict protein structures. Interpreting the diffusion generative model as a stochastic sampling process analogous to molec
papers.summary: The authors introduce an enhanced sampling method that adds a repulsive bias to AlphaFold3's diffusion-based structure prediction, allowing it to explore alternative protein conformations that standard AF3 often misses, such as ligand-induced conformational changes. By treating the diffusion model as a stochastic sampling process, they can generate a broader ensemble of plausible structures rather than a single predicted conformation.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study examines how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and related compounds may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease.

papers.title: CheckAMG: Accurate Identification of Auxiliary Viral Genes with Genome-Language Models.
papers.abstract: Viruses shape microbial metabolism through auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that reprogram host metabolism, physiology, and gene regulation during infection. Identifying AVGs is complicated by ambiguous viral versus cellular assignment, inconsistent curation, and reliance on sequence homology that misses divergent functions. Here we present CheckAMG, which pairs annotation-based AVG prediction, curated with a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic function, with a finetuned genome-language model for annotation-independent discovery. Benchmarked against DRAM-V and VIBRAN
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CheckAMG is a new tool that identifies auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) by combining annotation-based prediction with a fine-tuned genome-language model, addressing the difficulty of distinguishing viral from host genes and detecting divergent functions missed by homology-based methods. It uses a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic functions, and is benchmarked against existing tools DRAM-V and VIBRAN.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Multitask Framework Integrating Habitat and Deep Learning for Predicting Early Disease Control and Survival in Immunotherapy-Treated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients show heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study developed ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask network integrating CT-derived habitat and 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning features for simultaneously predicting early disease control (DC) and overall survival (OS). Of 1,234 patients with HCC enrolled from eight institutions and public databases, 832 ICI-treated patients were used for model development. ECOS-Net fused features using multi-head attention and generated early DC probabilities and OS risk scores. ECOS-DC a
papers.summary: This study introduces ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask deep learning framework that combines CT-derived habitat imaging features with 2.5D deep learning to simultaneously predict early disease control and overall survival in hepatocellular carcinoma patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Trained on 832 ICI-treated patients from eight institutions, the model aims to address heterogeneous treatment responses by integrating imaging and clinical data through multi-head attention.

papers.title: ASAS-NANP SYMPOSIUM: MATHEMATICAL MODELING IN ANIMAL NUTRITION: The Evolution of Large Language Models and Their Impact on Animal Sciences.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of large language models (LLM) is reshaping the scientific landscape, transitioning from early statistical language models to advanced transformer-based architectures capable of synthesizing knowledge across disciplines. While their predictive capacity and scalability have opened new avenues in data analysis, hypothesis generation, and decision support, concerns remain regarding bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance. In animal sciences, LLM are gradually applied to challenges in nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. Prec
papers.summary: This symposium paper reviews the evolution of large language models from early statistical approaches to modern transformer architectures and discusses their emerging applications in animal sciences, including nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. It also highlights key concerns such as bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance that must be addressed for responsible adoption.

papers.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design.
papers.abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence has produced a rapidly growing ecosystem of methods for de novo protein design. With access to many specialized and often complementary tools, how does one use them effectively, especially with a finite compute budget? Here, we introduce Target-adaptive Rescue-Explore-eXploit (T-REX) , an agentic protein binder design framework that orchestrates multiple state-of-the-art protein generative models and structure evaluators. Over the course of a design campaign, T-REX leverages large language model (LLM) agents to reason over accumulating outcomes and decide wh
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce T-REX, an agentic framework that uses LLM agents to orchestrate multiple protein generative models and structure evaluators for de novo binder design. T-REX adaptively decides which tools to use over the course of a design campaign, aiming to make efficient use of a finite compute budget. This represents an approach to automating and optimizing high-throughput protein design workflows.

papers.title: CardioChrom Reconstructs the Human Cardiac Virtual Epigenome from Single-Nucleus Transcriptomes.
papers.abstract: Matched epigenomic profiling remains scarce in human heart failure, limiting regulatory interpretation of single-nucleus ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing data. We developed CardioChrom, a cardiac-specialized framework that reconstructs chromatin accessibility, histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), and histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) from single-nucleus RNA profiles.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CardioChrom is a cardiac-specialized computational framework that reconstructs chromatin accessibility and histone modification states (H3K27ac, H3K27me3) directly from single-nucleus RNA sequencing data of human heart tissue. This addresses the scarcity of matched epigenomic profiling in heart failure studies, enabling regulatory interpretation of snRNA-seq datasets without requiring separate epigenomic assays.

papers.title: Multi-Granular Embedding and Hybrid Encoder-Decoder Architecture with Temporal Linear Regression Bypass for Sensor-Based Time Series Forecasting in Smart Infrastructure.
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a robust deep encoder-decoder neural network that integrates multiple deep sequence models for time series forecasting in sensor-based applications. The proposed approach features a sophisticated input embedding layer that integrates scalar features, position encodings, and multi-granularity time embeddings. To improve computational efficiency, we employ a generative-style decoder inspired by the Informer architecture, which enables full-length sequence prediction in a single iteration, avoiding the latency associated with traditional autoregressive models. The archite
papers.summary: The authors propose a deep encoder-decoder neural network for forecasting sensor-based time series in smart infrastructure, combining multiple deep sequence models with a multi-granularity input embedding layer and a generative-style decoder inspired by Informer. The architecture also includes a temporal linear regression bypass to improve accuracy and computational efficiency by predicting full sequences in a single pass.

papers.title: Combined Analysis of Transcriptome and Metabolome of Large-Size Triploid Rainbow Trout in Different Seasons.
papers.abstract: Seasonal temperature variation poses a significant physiological challenge for cold-water aquaculture species; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying seasonal adaptation in large-sized triploid rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we integrated liver transcriptomics and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics across four seasons (February, May, August, November) to investigate this phenomenon. Seasonal comparisons revealed pronounced molecular reprogramming, with the comparison between May and August showing the largest transcriptomic shift (13,359 di
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study integrated liver transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics in large triploid rainbow trout across four seasons to uncover molecular mechanisms of seasonal adaptation. The May-to-August transition showed the largest transcriptomic shift, indicating pronounced seasonal molecular reprogramming in this cold-water aquaculture species.

papers.title: ConFormer-Net: Spatiotemporal Modeling for Landslide Detection Using Multi-Temporal SAR Data.
papers.abstract: Landslides are characterized by sudden occurrence, severe destructiveness, and widespread spatial distribution. Therefore, rapid and accurate landslide detection is essential for reducing infrastructure damage and safeguarding human lives. Conventional landslide monitoring methods are generally time-consuming, labor-intensive, and inefficient, while existing deep learning-based landslide detection methods remain limited in multiscale spatial structure representation, temporal sequence modeling, and spatiotemporal feature fusion. To address these limitations, this study proposes ConFormer-Net,
papers.summary: ConFormer-Net is a deep learning architecture that combines convolutional neural networks with transformer-style attention to jointly model spatial and temporal patterns in multi-temporal SAR imagery for landslide detection. The method aims to improve multiscale spatial representation, temporal sequence modeling, and spatiotemporal feature fusion compared to existing deep learning approaches. It targets faster, more accurate landslide identification for disaster risk reduction.

papers.title: Protein eXplosion Imaging (PXI): Protein Structures from Laser-Driven Explosions.
papers.abstract: We investigate the structural information retained in the distribution of explosion ion trajectories from proteins subjected to strong ionization. Using molecular-dynamics simulations and machine-learning analysis benchmarked against an analytical approach, we show that low-resolution structural information can be retrieved from the explosion distributions alone. An ensemble of convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps recovers the radius of gyration and the three semi-axes of an ellipsoidal molecular envelope with prediction errors of 1.2 Å and 1.5 Å, respectively,
papers.summary: This paper explores whether structural information about proteins can be recovered from the ion trajectories produced when proteins are exploded by intense laser ionization. Using molecular dynamics simulations and convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps, the authors recover low-resolution shape parameters like radius of gyration and ellipsoidal semi-axes with errors around 1-1.5 Å. The work suggests a proof-of-concept for a new imaging modality, though it remains simulation-based and low-resolution.

papers.title: Self-supervised plasma proteomic representations for prospective disease prediction across varying protein availability.
papers.abstract: Large-scale plasma proteomics offers opportunities to characterize disease susceptibility and improve prospective risk prediction, but transferring proteomic predictors across datasets remains challenging because measured protein sets differ across cohorts, study phases and assay configurations. Here we developed a self-supervised protein-token Transformer that maps the proteins observed in each sample to a fixed-dimensional participant representation, allowing unavailable proteins to be omitted rather than imputed. Using plasma proteomic profiles from 53,014 participants in the UK Biobank Pha
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a self-supervised Transformer model that learns fixed-dimensional participant representations from plasma proteomic data by treating each measured protein as a token, allowing it to handle missing proteins without imputation. Applied to 53,014 UK Biobank participants, the approach enables prospective disease prediction and transfer of proteomic predictors across cohorts with differing protein panels.

papers.title: Predicting Capsid Protein Binding Sites in Single-Stranded RNA Viruses Using Machine Learning from Local Geometric Features.
papers.abstract: Selective recognition of viral RNA by capsid proteins is essential for genome packaging during the assembly of single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) viruses. However, identification of capsid protein binding sites in the RNA genome remains challenging because current experimental techniques are labor-intensive and low-throughput, motivating the development of computational approaches. Here, we present a sequence-based framework that integrates RNA tertiary structural modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict capsid protein binding sites. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational framework that combines RNA tertiary structure modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict where capsid proteins bind on single-stranded RNA viral genomes. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as a test case, the method aims to overcome the labor-intensive and low-throughput nature of experimental binding site identification. This offers a sequence-based approach for studying viral genome packaging.

papers.title: Predicting Supramolecular Self-Assembly of Peptide Structures with AlphaFold3.
papers.abstract: Self-assembled peptide-based nanostructures have diverse applications in the pharmaceutical and materials fields, but accurately predicting their self-assembly behavior without time-intensive organic synthesis and characterization remains a significant challenge. Here, we assess the effectiveness of AlphaFold3 (AF3), a deep learning model for protein structure prediction, in modeling peptide-based nanostructures and the interactions driving supramolecular self-assembly. We designed amphiphilic peptides composed of alternating hydrophobic residues (valine, leucine, isoleucine, phenylalanine) an
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint evaluates whether AlphaFold3 can predict the supramolecular self-assembly of designed amphiphilic peptides made of alternating hydrophobic residues. The authors test AF3's ability to model peptide nanostructures and the interactions driving their assembly, aiming to bypass time-intensive synthesis and characterization. It provides an early assessment of AF3's utility beyond single-protein structure prediction.

papers.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure.
papers.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files ra
papers.summary: dictyBase, the long-standing model organism database for Dictyostelium discoideum, has been completely reimplemented as a self-contained service built on static data files and minimal infrastructure. This redesign aims to reduce maintenance burden while preserving access to genomic data, protocols, stock center information, and community resources for researchers studying chemotaxis, development, and disease-relevant genes.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Anatomical and Learned Features in AI Models for Structural Brain MRI.
papers.abstract: In this work, we comprehensively evaluate three popular feature-extraction paradigms in AI-based neuroimaging modeling: (1) computation of anatomical surfaces and volumes, (2) supervised learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and (3) unsupervised pretraining of vision transformer (ViT) foundation models, followed by supervised finetuning. Our study is based on 18 publicly available datasets containing 3D structural T1-weighted MRI scans from approximately 80,000 participants across seven distinct clinical tasks. We observe that a linear model based on anatomical features matches t
papers.summary: This study compares three feature-extraction approaches for AI models on structural brain MRI: anatomical surface/volume measurements, supervised CNNs, and unsupervised pretrained ViT foundation models with supervised finetuning. Using 18 public datasets (~80,000 participants, seven clinical tasks), the authors find that a simple linear model based on anatomical features performs comparably to the more complex deep learning approaches.

papers.title: A Transferable Genomic Language Model Framework for Fungal Gene Essentiality Prediction.
papers.abstract: Predicting biological function from genomic sequence remains a major challenge in computational and systems biology. Here, we tested whether the genomic language model Evo2, which encodes context-dependent DNA sequence patterns into embeddings, enables prediction of essential genes in fungi, a phenotype central to fungal biology and antifungal target discovery. We found that model performance was constrained not by the type or complexity of the downstream classifier, but by the biological information contained in Evo2 DNA embeddings. Specifically, the information recoverable from these embeddi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study tests whether the genomic language model Evo2 can predict essential genes in fungi by encoding DNA sequence patterns into embeddings. The authors find that prediction performance is limited not by the downstream classifier but by the biological information contained in Evo2's DNA embeddings themselves. This suggests that current genomic language models may not capture sufficient functional information for reliable essentiality prediction.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts secreted effector proteins in Gram-negative bacteria by combining protein language model sequence embeddings with geometric features derived from predicted 3D structures. This structure-aware approach aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only methods and the scarcity of experimental structures, improving effector identification for understanding bacterial pathogenesis.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: SF-DTI is a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multiple protein encoders, aligns drug structure with semantic features, and progressively refines cross-modal representations. It aims to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein data while leveraging complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders.

papers.title: Dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding for anticancer peptide prediction via transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Computational identification of anti-tumor peptides (ACPs) is challenged by limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences. Standard transformer positional encodings fail to capture the periodicities and local motifs that govern peptide function. We propose dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), which replaces fixed sinusoidal encodings with parallel adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches, fused by a context-aware gating mechanism. A dual-stage transfer learning strategy pre-trains on 5,785 curated peptide sequences before fine-tuning on ACP74
papers.summary: The authors introduce dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), a transformer encoding scheme that combines adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches via context-aware gating to better capture periodicities and local motifs in peptide sequences. Using a dual-stage transfer learning strategy, they pre-train on 5,785 curated peptides and fine-tune for anticancer peptide prediction. This addresses limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences in ACP identification.

papers.title: Explainable AI-driven marker selection and development of EastFocus AISNPplex 61 assay for fine-scale biogeographical ancestry inference.
papers.abstract: A hierarchical ancestry inference framework was developed to resolve continental and fine-scale East Asian population structures for forensic applications. Combining the shapley additive explanations (SHAP) method with recursive feature elimination, 58 ancestry informative single-nucleotide polymorphisms (AIM-SNPs) were selected. A self-developed 6-dye allele-specific PCR multiplex system (EastFocus AISNPplex 61) was established, integrating these AIM-SNPs, two Y-chromosomal InDels, and the Amelogenin locus. Validation demonstrated reliable single-source genotyping down to 250-500 pg and full
papers.summary: This study developed an explainable AI framework combining SHAP and recursive feature elimination to select 58 ancestry-informative SNPs that resolve fine-scale East Asian population structure. These markers were incorporated into a 6-dye allele-specific PCR multiplex assay (EastFocus AISNPplex 61) alongside Y-chromosomal InDels and Amelogenin, validated for forensic use with reliable genotyping down to 250-500 pg of DNA.

papers.title: Omics data discovery agents: Agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g., protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs lar
papers.summary: The authors present an agentic framework that automatically retrieves, reanalyzes, and synthesizes published omics data scattered across papers, supplements, and repositories. The system aims to make the vast body of published omics studies computationally reusable, addressing the common problem that essential reproduction details are dispersed and intermediate data files are irregularly shared.

papers.title: Snail shell-derived hydroxyapatite on ant clay: a sustainable solution for phosphate sequestration and circular agricultural reuse.
papers.abstract: In this study, a sustainable adsorbent comprising hydroxyapatite derived from snail shells and clay collected from ant nests was developed and used for the efficient removal of phosphate (PO4 3-) from aqueous solutions. The synthesized adsorbent was characterized using different characterization techniques like FTIR spectroscopy, XRD, SEM, TGA, PZC, and BET analysis to confirm its successful synthesis, morphology, thermal stability, surface charges, and surface area, respectively. The adsorbent was systematically investigated for phosphate adsorption by optimizing key experimental parameters,
papers.summary: This study developed a sustainable phosphate adsorbent by combining hydroxyapatite derived from snail shells with clay from ant nests. The composite material was characterized and optimized for removing phosphate from water, supporting circular agricultural reuse of waste materials.

papers.title: Integrative multiomics and machine learning identify uridine as a candidate modulator of MMP7-mediated immune cell infiltration in pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrosing interstitial lung disease (ILD) characterized by immune cell infiltration and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Effective therapies remain limited. Uridine is an endogenous nucleoside with pro-reparative and immunomodulatory effects, but its molecular targets and immune mechanisms in IPF remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multiomics data with machine learning to identify uridine as a potential modulator of MMP7-mediated immune cell infiltration in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The work suggests a molecular link between uridine metabolism, MMP7 activity, and immune cell recruitment in IPF, highlighting a possible therapeutic target. However, the findings are based on computational and integrative analyses, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Serum Protein Panel Facilitates Surgical Decision-Making for Barcelona Stage B Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To develop a serum proteomic-based prognostic model for predicting surgical outcomes in BCLC stage B hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients, addressing the clinical heterogeneity that limits uniform treatment recommendations.
papers.summary: This study develops a serum proteomic-based prognostic model to predict surgical outcomes in Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage B hepatocellular carcinoma patients, a group with heterogeneous disease where treatment decisions are currently uniform. The panel aims to help clinicians identify which patients are likely to benefit from surgery, thereby refining surgical decision-making.

papers.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that clas
papers.summary: ProFormer is a transformer-based deep learning pipeline that directly classifies mass spectrometry proteomics data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identities. It is designed to work on both single-cell and plasma proteomes, addressing throughput limitations in large biological or clinical cohorts. The approach enables generalizable classification without extensive manual feature engineering.

papers.title: Discovery and Biological Characterization of 1-[4-(2-Difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A Novel Thiazolyl-Urea Chemotype Targeting Yellow Fever Virus and Host Casein Kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of DFMNTU, a novel thiazolyl-urea compound that targets both yellow fever virus and the host kinase CK2. The compound shows antiviral activity against YFV strain 17D in cell culture, suggesting host-directed antiviral potential. This represents an early-stage chemical biology finding with possible therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: This paper introduces pLM-HP, a machine learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones. It specifically addresses class imbalance, a common problem in this prediction task, and reports improved performance over existing methods. The tool aims to speed up identification of peptide hormones relevant to drug discovery.

papers.title: Progeny Differentiation in Faba Bean Using Hyperspectral Images and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Though currently a minor crop, faba bean is a promising source of plant-based protein as global diets shift towards more plant-based nutrition. To realize this potential, advances in breeding and cultivation are crucial. To exploit heterosis, faba bean breeding frequently utilizes synthetic cultivars, produced by open pollination of inbred lines, resulting in a mixture of F1 hybrid seeds and self-pollinated offspring. Pure F1 hybrid cultivars are currently unavailable due to unstable cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) systems. An ability to distinguish F1 seeds from their parental inbreds based
papers.summary: This study uses hyperspectral imaging combined with machine learning to distinguish F1 hybrid seeds from self-pollinated offspring in faba bean breeding. The approach could help breeders identify true hybrids without relying on unstable cytoplasmic male sterility systems, supporting more efficient exploitation of heterosis in this emerging plant-protein crop.

papers.title: Information Leakage in Enzyme Substrate Prediction.
papers.abstract: Enzymes are essential catalysts in many cellular processes. Understanding their interactions with small molecules, such as regulators, cofactors, and most importantly, substrates, is crucial for understanding the biochemical processes that occur in cells. Correctly interpreting the roles of small molecules that interact with enzymes is key to elucidating enzyme function. Recently, enzyme-small molecule interaction prediction has attracted growing interest from computational methods, especially deep learning. As a result, researchers have published several datasets and numerous models with rema
papers.summary: This paper investigates information leakage in deep learning models for predicting enzyme-substrate interactions, showing that common dataset construction and evaluation practices can inflate performance estimates. The authors likely demonstrate that models may exploit trivial correlations or overlapping data rather than learning genuine biochemical signals, and they propose guidelines to avoid such pitfalls. The work serves as a cautionary methodological critique for computational enzyme function prediction.

papers.title: Progressive remodeling of global protein interaction networks in a mouse model of tauopathy.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disease is marked not just by loss of proteins or cells, but by dynamic rewiring of macromolecular interaction networks that precede and drive pathology. Here, we present a temporally resolved, systems-scale map of multi-protein complex remodeling in a tauopathy model, integrating co-fractionation mass spectrometry, quantitative phosphoproteomics, and machine learning to decode phosphorylation-dependent shifts in protein interactomes across disease progression. This interactomic atlas serves as a resource to investigate functional assemblies, including MAPT-Dpysl2 and Cyfip1-
papers.summary: This study maps how protein interaction networks progressively rewire over the course of tauopathy in a mouse model, using co-fractionation mass spectrometry, quantitative phosphoproteomics, and machine learning. The authors generate a temporally resolved interactomic atlas revealing phosphorylation-dependent shifts in multi-protein complexes, including assemblies like MAPT-Dpysl2 and Cyfip1-containing complexes. This resource links dynamic network remodeling to disease progression before overt pathology.

papers.title: Beyond affinity: AI-supported developability assessment and multi-objective optimization in antibody development.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies are a major class of medicines, but high target affinity alone does not ensure manufacturability, stability, safety, or clinical success. Developability has therefore become a central constraint in antibody engineering and has pushed the field beyond affinity-first screening toward multi-objective decision-making. Machine-learning-based models increasingly integrate antibody sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to estimate properties such as affinity, specificity, aggregation, viscosity, solubility, stability, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetics before exper
papers.summary: This review discusses how therapeutic antibody development is shifting from a singular focus on target affinity toward multi-objective optimization of developability properties like stability, solubility, and immunogenicity. It highlights how machine-learning models integrate sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to predict these properties before experimental testing, enabling more efficient selection of viable drug candidates.

papers.title: A dual-tower multimodal framework with feature quality enhancement for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Pathological complete response (pCR) is a key endpoint following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer, with potential to guide treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation. However, limited generalizability across institutions remains a major challenge due to heterogeneous imaging protocols (scanner vendors, field strengths, and acquisition parameters) and diverse patient populations, which can cause significant domain shifts in model performance. This study develops and externally validates a multimodal framework for post-neoadjuvant, preoperative prediction of pCR using multipa
papers.summary: This study develops a dual-tower multimodal deep learning framework that integrates imaging and clinical data to predict pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer patients. The framework includes feature quality enhancement to address domain shifts caused by heterogeneous imaging protocols across institutions, and it is externally validated in a multicenter setting. The approach aims to improve generalizability and support treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation decisions.

papers.title: Network pharmacology, single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning and experimental validation identifying CHEK2 and HPGD as key therapeutic targets of berberine in diabetic nephropathy.
papers.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a severe microvascular complication of diabetes with limited therapeutic options. Berberine exhibits renoprotective potential, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanisms of action in DN remain unclear. Berberine targets were retrieved from TCMSP, SEA, and SwissTargetPrediction databases. Bulk transcriptomic microarray datasets (GSE96804, GSE30122) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset (GSE131882) were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) wer
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify CHEK2 and HPGD as key targets through which berberine may protect against diabetic nephropathy. Experimental validation supports these targets, suggesting a mechanistic basis for berberine's renoprotective effects.

papers.title: Gut microbiota signatures and machine learning-based candidate feature prioritization in advanced colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: This single-center, cross-sectional case-control study aimed to characterize the gut microbiome profiles of patients with advanced colorectal cancer (CRC), identify candidate microbial features, and explore how well these features distinguished advanced CRC cases from healthy controls within the study dataset. Fecal samples were collected from 72 treatment-naïve patients with advanced CRC and 61 healthy controls. Microbial community structure was profiled using high-throughput sequencing of the V3-V4 region of the 16 S rRNA gene. The analytical pipeline included α/β-diversity analysis, multile
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study profiled the gut microbiome of 72 treatment-naïve advanced colorectal cancer patients and 61 healthy controls using 16S rRNA sequencing, finding distinct microbial community structures between groups. Machine learning was then applied to prioritize candidate microbial features that best distinguished advanced CRC cases from controls within the dataset.

papers.title: Rethinking input complexity in transformer-based clinical prediction: implications for feature dimensionality and sequence length in longitudinal electronic health record data.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based models for clinical prediction using longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data are often developed with large feature sets and long patient histories under the assumption that more data improves performance. However, high-dimensional inputs and long sequences increase computational burden, potentially limiting scalability. We evaluated how feature dimensionality and sequence length affect predictive performance, calibration, risk stratification, and computational efficiency in EHR prediction.
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates how the number of input features and the length of patient history sequences affect transformer-based clinical prediction models trained on longitudinal EHR data. It finds that increasing input complexity does not consistently improve performance and can harm calibration and efficiency, suggesting that smaller, more focused inputs may be preferable.

papers.title: Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer: A Novel Approach for Multi-Objective De Novo Drug Design.
papers.abstract: Designing novel molecules that simultaneously satisfy several, often conflicting, properties is a long-standing challenge in drug design. While recent deep learning advances optimize single targets effectively, navigating the trade-offs required for multiple objectives remains a difficult problem.
papers.summary: The authors propose the Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer (MOC-RB-DT), a novel deep learning architecture for de novo drug design that aims to generate molecules satisfying multiple, often conflicting, properties simultaneously. The approach extends decision transformer methods with return-block conditioning to better navigate multi-objective trade-offs, addressing a key limitation of existing single-target optimization models.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of mitochondrial proteomes across the tree of life.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria arose from the endosymbiosis of a bacterium with an archaea-related host cell about 2 billion years ago. To understand their origins and evolution, we compared experimentally defined mitoproteomes from the MitoCarta Tree of Life project. Across eight organisms, we identified 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins within 3,199 families, of which 43% lack Pfam domains. We report 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens yet absent in humans, representing promising candidate targets for protozoan infectious diseases. Leveraging our experimentally defined mitoproteomes, we
papers.summary: This study compares experimentally defined mitochondrial proteomes across eight organisms spanning the tree of life, identifying 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins in 3,199 families, 43% of which lack known Pfam domains. The authors highlight 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens but absent in humans, offering potential drug targets for protozoan infectious diseases.

papers.title: Integrating Multimodal MRI Habitat and Transformer-Based Pathomics to Predict High-Risk Molecular Subtypes and Explore Biological Mechanisms in Adult Diffuse Gliomas.
papers.abstract: This study aims to achieve accurate prediction of high-risk molecular subtypes of gliomas through a cross-scale Combined model, matching the model's classification metrics with patient risk stratification and exploring the underlying biological mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study develops a cross-scale combined model that integrates multimodal MRI habitat imaging with transformer-based pathomics to predict high-risk molecular subtypes in adult diffuse gliomas. The model's classification performance is linked to patient risk stratification, and the authors explore the underlying biological mechanisms driving these predictions. This work demonstrates how combining radiology and pathology data through deep learning can improve molecular subtyping of gliomas.

papers.title: A Deep-Learning Based Biomarker of Systemic Cellular Senescence Burden to Predict Mortality and Health Outcomes.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of senescent cells is a recognized hallmark of biological aging and is associated with the onset of multiple chronic medical conditions. Senescent cells exhibit a distinct secretory profile, known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which can propagate cellular senescence to neighboring and distant tissues. Measuring SASP factors in blood serves as a practical proxy for cellular senescence burden and may help track disease states and intervention outcomes. We developed and validated a composite SASP Score by integrating large-scale population proteomics da
papers.summary: The authors developed a deep-learning-derived composite SASP Score by integrating large-scale population proteomics data to quantify systemic cellular senescence burden from blood. This biomarker was validated as a predictor of mortality and adverse health outcomes, offering a practical tool for tracking aging and intervention effects.

papers.title: Autoimmune disorders and cardiovascular disease: a matched cross-sectional analysis of disease-specific associations in Qatari primary care.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune disorders have been linked to increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, but it is unclear whether the association is uniform across conditions or is concentrated in specific diseases, and whether inflammatory markers add value in a Middle Eastern primary-care setting. We examined disease-specific associations between autoimmune disorders and recorded CVD, rather than building a prognostic prediction tool.
papers.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study examined whether the link between autoimmune disorders and cardiovascular disease varies by specific autoimmune condition in a Qatari primary-care population, using matched analysis. The authors found disease-specific associations rather than a uniform risk across all autoimmune disorders, and assessed whether inflammatory markers add predictive value.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review critically examines how artificial intelligence—including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models—can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while these approaches offer new opportunities, much of the evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation.

papers.title: Efficacy and exploratory treatment-response modeling of acupuncture for acute migraine based on DIA proteomics: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: According to estimates from the 2019 Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study, approximately 1.1 billion people worldwide suffer from migraine, with a prevalence rate of about 14% to 15%. Despite the development of various medications for different types of migraine, such as acetaminophen and caffeine combination preparations, most patients still experience suboptimal symptom control. Therefore, identifying effective and safer alternative treatments holds significant clinical importance. Acupuncture was formally recommended by the World Health Organization as a migraine therapy as early as 1979. I
papers.summary: This paper presents a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial testing acupuncture as a treatment for acute migraine, using DIA (data-independent acquisition) proteomics to explore treatment-response biomarkers. The goal is to assess efficacy while identifying protein signatures that may predict or explain individual responses to acupuncture.

papers.title: Exploring the key genes of colorectal "adenoma-cancer" based on graph transformer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, and the precise identification of biomarkers from colonic adenoma to cancer is of great significance for preventing the development of adenocarcinoma. Given that existing methods inadequately capture the topological network relationships among genes, this study proposes a graph neural network model based on multifeature learning, named ChebTs, to investigate the correlation between key genes involved in the colorectal "adenoma-cancer" transition. The GSE41657 and GSE31905 datasets from the GEO database were stratified in
papers.summary: This study introduces ChebTs, a graph transformer-based neural network model that integrates multiple gene features to identify key genes driving the transition from colorectal adenoma to cancer. Using GEO datasets GSE41657 and GSE31905, the model aims to better capture topological gene network relationships than existing methods, potentially improving biomarker discovery for early CRC prevention.

papers.title: Mechanism-aware and safety-validated AI for drug repurposing: a critical review and translational pharmacology framework.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted drug repurposing seeks to identify new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Nevertheless, most of the existing studies are centered on prediction scores and candidate ranking, and there is still relatively little attention paid to the pharmacological mechanisms, safety and translational validation.
papers.summary: This critical review argues that AI-driven drug repurposing has focused too heavily on prediction scores and candidate ranking while neglecting pharmacological mechanism validation, safety assessment, and translational testing. The authors propose a translational pharmacology framework that integrates mechanism-awareness and safety validation into AI repurposing pipelines.

papers.title: From surveillance to intelligence: a scoping review of machine learning for antimicrobial resistance surveillance intelligence across One Health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a leading global health threat requiring coordinated surveillance across human, animal, environmental, and genomic systems. Machine learning is increasingly applied to AMR data, yet its contribution to actionable surveillance intelligence, rather than prediction alone, remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how machine learning is being applied to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance data across human, animal, environmental, and genomic domains within a One Health framework. It argues that most current ML efforts focus narrowly on prediction rather than generating actionable surveillance intelligence, and it maps the gaps between data-driven modeling and real-world decision-making.

papers.title: Surveillance-Driven Machine Learning for Prediction of Antimicrobial Susceptibility: An Explainable Modeling Framework using the Pfizer ATLAS Dataset (2004 - 2023).
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global public health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where delayed antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) and limited diagnostic capacity complicate timely treatment and antimicrobial stewardship (AMS). Although large-scale surveillance programmes routinely collect antimicrobial susceptibility data, these datasets remain underutilised for predictive analytics.
papers.summary: This paper develops an explainable machine learning framework that predicts antimicrobial susceptibility using 20 years of surveillance data from the Pfizer ATLAS dataset (2004-2023). The approach aims to support antimicrobial stewardship and treatment decisions, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where timely susceptibility testing is often unavailable.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified human-mouse shared gene space using supervised contrastive learning, then predicts transcription factor-target regulatory relationships from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression via a multi-relational heterograph to address noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts in GRN inference.

papers.title: Radiomics and deep learning for immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes: imaging-derived immune phenotyping and clinical translation across solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of multiple solid tumors, but durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients and conventional size-based imaging does not fully capture immune-related response patterns. Radiomics and deep learning offer a route to convert routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT into quantitative biomarkers of tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence across solid tumors with an emphasis on four questions that are often separated in the literature: what
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on using radiomics and deep learning to predict immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes across solid tumors, framing imaging as a tool for non-invasive immune phenotyping. It emphasizes four key questions often treated separately in the literature, covering tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response from routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT. The review aims to bridge technical imaging biomarkers with clinical translation for patient selection and response monitoring.

papers.title: Explainable growth stage classification of cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) leaves and key feature visualization using vision transformer and transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate and objective plant phenotyping is crucial for optimizing agricultural practices, understanding plant development, and enabling rapid responses to environmental changes. Traditional methods, often relying on visual observation, can be subjective, time-consuming, and may overlook subtle but important differences. This study demonstrates the power of combining digital imaging with deep learning to classify plant material with high accuracy, even when visual differences are minimal. We focused on differentiating between stage D (light green) and stage E (dark green) leaves of cacao (Theo
papers.summary: This study applies a vision transformer with transfer learning to classify cacao leaves into two closely related growth stages (D and E) based on subtle color differences, achieving high accuracy where visual inspection is difficult. The authors also visualize key features driving the model's decisions, making the classification explainable. The work demonstrates how deep learning can support objective, automated plant phenotyping in agriculture.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Stem Cell Research: From Biological Data to Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Stem cell (SC) research plays a central role in disease modeling and regenerative medicine, yet its clinical translation remains challenged by biological heterogeneity, incomplete cellular maturation, stringent quality-control requirements, and increasingly complex biological and clinical data. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for extracting biologically meaningful information from these data, enabling quantitative characterization of SC behavior and predictive modeling across diverse experimental and translational applications. This review presents a unif
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across stem cell research, from analyzing complex biological data to supporting clinical translation. It highlights ML's role in quantitatively characterizing stem cell behavior and building predictive models despite challenges like heterogeneity and quality control. The paper provides a unified overview of current methods and translational applications.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence Multimorbidity Score for Human-Machine Clinical Risk Stratification.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is strongly associated with mortality, but existing comorbidity indices often generalize poorly across populations because they depend on fixed disease lists and context-specific weights. We developed the large-language-model-based multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity phenotype score, as a bio-inspired artificial intelligence score for human-machine clinical risk stratification and evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts. Harmonized participant-level data wer
papers.summary: The authors developed LLM-MMS, a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity score, as a bio-inspired AI tool for clinical risk stratification. They evaluated its ability to predict all-cause mortality in 770,439 adults across 9 international longitudinal cohorts, aiming to overcome the poor generalizability of fixed disease-list comorbidity indices.
